Subject: Marketplace pricing grid & budget — follow-up (private offer mapping)

Hi Lee / Atlas team,

Thanks again for taking time today — good call. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can map a private offer on the marketplace and validate unit economics: 

Call recap (short):
- Workload: user-facing clinical summarization + search re-ranker. Avg prompt length ~150 tokens, generation ~300 tokens.
- Expected concurrency: bursts to 120 qps during peak morning window; sustained ~20 qps off-peak.
- Annual target volume: roughly 1.2B generation tokens + 400M embed tokens.
- Primary constraint: procurement needs a marketplace private-offer with a clear $/1M tokens unit to compare against internal P&L.

Action items (proposed):
1) You confirm the 12–18 month committed budget bands (low/medium/high).
2) We produce a pricing grid that maps Redwood hosted unit price to an equivalent private-offer unit (AWS/GCP/Azure) including marketplace fees and reserving assumptions.
3) We share an example private-offer spreadsheet and a short FAQ for procurement.

Requested from you: please confirm rough annual budget range (bands are fine) and whether Atlas requires a single flat unit price or tiered buckets by monthly committed tokens.

I'll loop in Dev and Rishi for the unit-econ mapping and will attach an initial template for Atlas to review early next week.

Best,

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference

Vanessa — thanks for the recap. Helpful. A few clarifications from procurement side: 

1) Budget bands (annual committed spend):
   - Low: $250k–$500k
   - Mid: $500k–$1.25M
   - High: $1.25M+
2) Prefer a tiered bucket model (monthly buckets) that soft-commits to a baseline with overflow at a higher unit price. Single flat price is harder for internal approvals.
3) Target benchmark: we need an internal comparison to ~ $900–1,200 per 1M generation tokens (this is what our treasury team used for recent models).

Also: the marketplace team prefers price components to be explicit (base unit, marketplace % fee, any setup/one-time). If you can map Redwood hosted unit --> AWS Marketplace private-offer unit (inc. 12% marketplace fee example) that would be perfect.

I'll loop back if procurement needs a specific contract template.

Thanks,
Lee Carter
Head of Procurement (Atlas Health)
lee.carter@atlashealth.com

Hi Lee / Atlas team — attaching the pricing grid we discussed and a short note on assumptions. High-level summary below, details in attached spreadsheet.

Summary (effective $/1M generation tokens):
- Low bucket (annual commit: $250k–$500k): Redwood hosted equivalent $1,050 / 1M --> Marketplace private-offer example: $1,176 / 1M (assumes 12% marketplace fee, no long-term reserved discount)
- Mid bucket (annual commit: $500k–$1.25M): Redwood hosted equivalent $920 / 1M --> Marketplace private-offer example: $1,030 / 1M (assumes partial 6-month commit discount applied)
- High bucket (annual commit: $1.25M+): Redwood hosted equivalent $780 / 1M --> Marketplace private-offer example: $873 / 1M (assumes 12-month reserved commit discount and volume tiers)

Assumptions (short):
- Token mix: 75% generation, 25% embedding/re-ranker tokens using Atlas-provided ratios.
- Marketplace fee: 12% (example; actual differs by cloud).
- Reserved discount: modeled at 8–12% depending on commit length; applied to base hosted unit.
- Overflow: billed at hosted unit * 1.15 (example overflow premium) then marketplace fee applies.

Next steps:
- Lee: confirm whether Atlas prefers the 12% marketplace fee estimate or needs cloud-specific numbers (AWS vs GCP vs Azure).
- Vanessa: can we schedule a 30-min procurement walkthrough next Tue (23rd) or Wed (24th)?
- We'll publish the attached RI_Private_Offer_Pricing_Grid.xlsx and a one-page FAQ to the shared Drive.

Thanks — happy to walk through any row-level numbers.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Commercial Strategy, Redwood Inference

Attachments: RI_Private_Offer_Pricing_Grid.xlsx (spreadsheet)
